findings.where: The full-width blue 'Get Mark's briefings on PPP reform' band and its white 'Subscribe' button, just below the hero (desktop-02 top; on the phone, directly under the email action)
findings.fault: Subscribe looks like a working button, but it only jumps to #subscribe. The page has no subscribe form, sign-up or anything else at that target, so the click does nothing useful. The band is also a second call to action and the boldest block of colour after the hero. On the phone it sits right under 'Write to me directly', so it competes with the page's one action, getting in touch with Mark, and draws the eye away from it.
findings.who_objects: A development-bank officer who taps Subscribe expecting to sign up for briefings gets nothing back and may think the site is broken or unfinished. Mark (through the founder) would object too: the brief allows one direct, personal way to reach him, and this band offers a subscription that doesn't exist.

findings.where: The header across the hero: the 'Mark M. Moseley' name and the MMM Infra logo, at desktop and phone
findings.fault: The homepage has no navigation. The only working part of the header is the logo, which goes back to the top of the same page. Nothing leads to Mark's articles, his PDFs, an about page or contact. The palette even lists 'nav links' in mist on slate, but none are on the page. The brief's first screen calls for a nav.
findings.who_objects: A visitor who wants to read Mark's work or check his background before writing to him can't see where those are or how to reach them. The founder would object because the brief sets the first screen as 'nav, logo, Mark's line, his photograph, one action'.

findings.where: The article specimen's lecture card, 'Streamlining the PPP Process: Meeting the 'Abundance' Challenge', with its download arrow and 'PDF' label
findings.fault: The card says it is a PDF download (a download arrow and the word PDF), but the link only goes to #article on the same page. Nothing downloads and no document opens, so the card shows one action and does another.
findings.who_objects: A reader who clicks to save Mark's lecture gets no file and has to guess whether it's missing. Per the research the PDF list is part of the product, so a card whose download sign doesn't download weakens the depth visitors scroll down for.

findings.where: Blue on parts that can't be clicked: the article list's numbers 1–3, the tracked blue 'PALETTE' eyebrow, and the blue 'MMM INFRA' wordmark in the footer that sits next to the blue footer email link
findings.fault: The page's own note says 'blue only where something can be clicked', and blue is the link colour throughout. Yet the list numbers and the PALETTE label are blue and do nothing. Under the footer mark, the blue wordmark looks the same as the blue email link beside it. Blue therefore means both 'click here' and 'just text'.
findings.who_objects: A reader of the article page (Angélique's articles will repeat this list style on every page) may try clicking blue numbers or labels, and learns blue isn't a reliable sign of a link, which makes the real links harder to trust.

findings.where: The 'Replay the opening' control under the motion sketch
findings.fault: It is a button that replays the animation in place, but it looks exactly like the page's links (blue and underlined). Nothing on the page tells the visitor whether it will run something here or take them somewhere else.
findings.who_objects: A keyboard or screen-reader user, or anyone used to the link look, expects it to go to another page. It is a small mismatch on a specimen control, but it breaks the rule that one look means one function.

findings.where: The header lockup: 'Mark M. Moseley' beside the MMM Infra logo, separated by a hairline
findings.fault: The logo is a home link, but Mark's name next to it, in the same header in a light, link-like colour, does nothing. The two halves of one lockup behave differently.
findings.who_objects: A visitor who clicks the name to get home, as most sites allow, gets no response. Few would notice, since the logo beside it works.
